clue.text: Man with libertine cavorting without end

indicators.note: cavorting is prancing about wildly, so the letters of the two words caper into a new order

explanation.surface: A man keeps company with a debauched rake, the pair frolicking on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges MAN and LIBERTINE together; 'without end' looks like part of the scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interminable never seems to stop, which is what 'without end' describes.

clue.text: Current reportedly made hole contained by ship

parts.note: current in the sense of fashionable or in vogue

indicators.note: reportedly says we only hear the next word, so its spoken form stands in for the written one

parts.note: to make a hole by drilling is to bore, past tense bored

explanation.surface: Electrical current, it seems, drilled a hole inside a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts toward I or AC, but here it means trendy. BORED and BOARD are spoken alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Inboard describes something situated within the hull of a vessel, the opposite of outboard.

clue.text: Initially tests resolve over treacherous husband's fidelity

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A betrayed spouse's loyalty is put to the test by a cheating husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Troth is an old word for faithfulness or a pledged promise, as in 'plight one's troth'.

clue.text: Sort of energy helping to keep support up

indicators.note: to keep means the portion holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a helping is a portion or ration of food

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Some kind of energy assists in propping up a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like an adjective with 'energy'; it is a noun, a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiation is energy emitted as waves or particles, so it is one kind of energy.

clue.text: Country yours truly led

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, the speaker, hence I
to lead an organisation is to run it; past tense ran

explanation.surface: The speaker boasts of having once been in charge of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Even American clubs score to catch United

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: to catch means the score word grabs and holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: a tally is a running score or count
U is a standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: American golf clubs score points, perhaps enough to catch a team called United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts U inside TALLY, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and actually both work as intensifiers meaning 'in fact', as in 'he even/actually apologised'.

clue.text: Composer's record for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, so the spoken word is what counts

parts.note: a list is a written record of items

explanation.surface: A composer's recording is made for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'). Franz Liszt was the Hungarian virtuoso pianist-composer; his name and LIST are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Liszt was a celebrated nineteenth-century Hungarian composer of piano works and tone poems.

clue.text: Tremendous lovers I zealously embraced

indicators.note: embraced means held within the run of words, so the letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: A passionate lover recalls zealously hugging their partners in a huge way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something unusually large; oversize means bigger than normal, like tremendous.

clue.text: Open a French drink upended

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: upended, in a down clue, means turned upside down so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a gulp is a big swallow of drink

explanation.surface: Uncorking a French bottle and tipping it up to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug a blocked drain or sink is to clear it, making it open again.

clue.text: Circulated around street on minor route

indicators.note: on here means the street-and-around pair is placed after the minor route word

parts.note: a B road is a secondary road in Britain, below an A road
ca, short for circa, means around or approximately

explanation.surface: Something went the rounds, passing a street on a little-used back road.
explanation.walkthrough: A B road is a British secondary road, the class below main A roads.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news or a rumour is to spread it widely, so circulated is a synonym.

clue.text: Number understood to be about five?

indicators.note: to be about means the first word surrounds the numeral

parts.note: seen in the sense of grasped, as in 'I see what you mean'
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A figure is taken to be roughly five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be about' wraps SEEN around V. The question mark flags that seven is not literally about five.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a cardinal number, one more than six, so it is an example of a number.

clue.text: Hermitage made from wood and stuff

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
to ram is to cram or stuff something in

explanation.surface: A hermit's retreat built out of timber and other materials.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a secluded religious retreat in India, a place of withdrawal like a hermit's dwelling.

clue.text: Priestly ancient using speech

parts.note: ancient times are long past
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A clerical elder who communicates by talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral relates to a pastor's care for his flock, so it means relating to the clergy.

clue.text: Nudist, ill-mannered, keeping press out

indicators.note: keeping means the words hold the answer inside them across the comma

explanation.surface: A rude naturist refuses to be pressed into leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To distil is to extract an essence, much as squeezing something draws out its juice.

clue.text: Working at a diet's getting stuffed

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone toiling at a diet still ends up full.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiated means filled to the point of having had enough, which is being stuffed after a meal.

clue.text: Thrashing without holding top of lash

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the next letter inside it

parts.note: failing in the sense of lacking, as in 'failing that'

indicators.note: top of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A beating administered without even using the whip's tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is not a deletion signal here: it means FAILING. 'top of' gives L, which 'holding' puts inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flailing means waving the limbs about wildly, the same movement as thrashing.

clue.text: Still stupid tackling one on rug

indicators.note: tackling means the first word takes on and wraps around the following pieces

parts.note: inane means silly or senseless
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A daft fellow wrestling someone on a rug, who is still lying there.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless or motionless, which is one sense of still.

clue.text: Unbroken channel round outskirts of Greenwich

indicators.note: round means the channel word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a strait is a narrow sea channel

indicators.note: outskirts of points to the outermost letters of the place name

explanation.surface: An unbroken waterway runs around the edge of Greenwich in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives G and H, which STRAIT goes 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight run is continuous and uninterrupted, as in 'five straight wins', so unbroken.

clue.text: Let off partner accepting rejected attention

indicators.note: accepting means the partner word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a date is a romantic partner for an evening

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: note means attention or notice, as in 'take note'

explanation.surface: A partner forgives the snub of being ignored and lets someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' reads as pardon in the surface, but it means set off explosively.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off a bomb or firework is to set it exploding, the meaning of detonate.

clue.text: Run away from heartless fool perhaps

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: a fool is a British pudding of fruit and cream, so an example of a sweet course

explanation.surface: Escaping from some cruel idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' tempts as a person; it is a fruit-and-cream pudding. 'heartless' takes the middle S out of DESSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to abandon them, leaving or running away from them.

clue.text: Film-maker possibly approached artist

parts.note: came as in drew near
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A movie director, perhaps, came up to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film-maker' tempts toward a director; the device itself makes the film.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera literally makes film images, so it is a playful example of a film-maker.

clue.text: Shock purchasing occasionally free clothing

indicators.note: purchasing means the shock word acquires and holds the letters inside

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify

indicators.note: occasionally takes only some letters, here every other one of the word

explanation.surface: Horror at being charged for clothes that should be free.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments, so it means clothing.

clue.text: Continue circling sky with flight

indicators.note: circling means the first word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to stay is to remain or continue, as in 'stay the course'
the air is the sky above

explanation.surface: An aircraft keeps circling the sky on its flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a run of stairs between floors, which a stairway is.

clue.text: Sap is wrong supporting rise of Queen

indicators.note: supporting means, in a down clue, coming beneath the other piece
rise of means, in a down clue, that the letters go upward and so read backwards

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
a sin is a wrong or misdeed

explanation.surface: A fool is mistaken in backing the Queen's ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' tempts as a fool; it is tree sap. 'rise of' gives RE, with SIN placed under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky substance that oozes from trees, a kind of sap.

clue.text: Unfinished figure on motorway creates accident

indicators.note: on here means the trimmed figure word is placed after the motorway letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, read as MI

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a figure is a shape or form

explanation.surface: An incomplete road sign on a motorway leads to a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to Yorkshire, written MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky incident, a minor accident.

clue.text: Raise army to protect island

indicators.note: to protect means the army word surrounds and shields the letter

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude

explanation.surface: An army is raised to defend an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to lift up, especially with ropes, so it means to raise.

clue.text: List of soldiers with uniform

parts.note: men means ordinary soldiers, the ranks
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A roster of troops along with their uniform details.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list, whether of dishes in a restaurant or options on a screen.

clue.text: River fish potentially found in rocks

parts.note: eels are an example of fish, hence the hedge

explanation.surface: Some river fish may be discovered among stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like stones; it is a verb meaning sways.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or sway, and to rock is to sway to and fro, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Guardsman turned out in red gear?

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A soldier on parade, dressed in scarlet kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grenadier Guards wear the familiar red tunics at Buckingham Palace, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier of the Grenadier Guards, one of the British Army's Foot Guards.

clue.text: Altering manner, lutist produces musical piece

indicators.note: altering means the letters are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: A lute player changes style and turns out a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumental is a piece of music played without singing, so a musical piece.
